Use the model above to determine the missing number in the equation below.

$$
\frac{7}{12}÷\frac{3}{4}=\frac{\boxed{\,\,}}{9}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The denominators are $12$ and $4.$ We can make a common denominator of $12$ by splitting the shape on the right into $3$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14155061/assets/1d05074d23c48a2ff9604d5a1aec5521c0fb043ebeed9424f7182e480404771d.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{7}{12}÷\frac{9}{12}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
7÷9=\frac{7}{9}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{7}{12}÷\frac{3}{4}=\frac{\boxed{\,7\,}}{9}\,.
$$

Therefore, the missing number is $7.$
